prerequisites: At least 60 ECTS credits from basic training module and common industrial branch module (first and second year) courses must be passed.
Applied Mechanics, mastering: concepts related to static equilibrium, obtaining section forces (axial, shear and bending) and establishing force diagrams.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.

Know, understand and apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids, enabling the student for the subsequent application of advanced methods and theories in their professional development in areas of mechanical engineering and also providing them with great versatility to adapt to new situations.

Adequately apply the strategies of the scientific methodology to the problems posed by structural systems and deformable solids: analyze the situation qualitatively and quantitatively, propose hypotheses and solutions to solve problems typical of mechanical engineering.

Express, using appropriate means, theoretical knowledge, resolution methods, results and inherent aspects of the problems posed by the equilibrium of deformable solids and structural systems, using specific vocabulary and terminology.
Work effectively in groups, integrating abilities and knowledge to formulate ideas, debate proposals and make decisions in the development of work specific to elasticity and strength of materials.
Perform measurements, calculations, studies, reports and other similar works related to problematic situations that may arise in the field of elasticity and strength of materials.

syllabus_topics: General considerations. Scope of the subject.
Components: Elasticity and Strength of Materials.
Strength of Materials in the design process of a mechanical engineering work.
Hypotheses on the nature of bodies under study.
Shear stress (or tangential) and angular deformation.
Plane states of stress and strain.
Plane elasticity. Plane strain state. Mohr's circle.
Maximum principal stress criterion or Rankine criterion.
Maximum strain theory or Saint-Venant criterion.
Maximum shear stress theory or Tresca criterion.
The prismatic piece. Forces and deformations. Navier's hypothesis.
Stress state in simple tension or compression.
Deformations in simple tension or compression.
Effect of temperature and pre-strains or pre-stresses.
General theory of bending. Stresses I.
Combined bending and torsion in circular shafts.
General theory of bending. Stresses II.
Field of application of Euler's formula.
Degree of hyperstaticity and static redundants.
Introduction to the study of rigid-jointed structures.
Stresses and deformations in spatial structures.

assessment_methods.method: Completion of practical exercises (exercises, cases or problems)

assessment_rules: Assessment is based on four partial exams and a final exam. An average grade above 5.0 across the four partial exams is required to pass the course. Each partial exam covers a specific part of the course and allows exemption from the corresponding part of the final exam, provided a minimum of 40% of the maximum score is achieved in that partial exam. Students have three opportunities (during the semester, ordinary, and extraordinary calls) to pass these partial exams.
